style.vernacular: Dense lagoon-side metropolis: concrete-block compounds and walk-up flats of 1-4 storeys, plastered and painted in faded pastels, under rusty or coloured corrugated-iron roofs; Afro-Brazilian stucco buildings with arched windows on the Island; glass-and-concrete towers on Victoria Island; high perimeter walls with razor wire, generator sheds and water tanks.

style.vernacular: Brick city: yellow London stock-brick Georgian and Regency terraces with white stucco and sash windows; red-brick Victorian and Edwardian terraces with bay windows and terracotta; 1930s tile-hung semis; post-war concrete and brick estates and slab blocks; glass towers in the City and Docklands. Pitched slate or clay-tile roofs with chimney stacks, and plane and oak street trees.
style.ornament: Georgian double-hung sash windows with white frames and stucco quoins and cornices; Victorian polychrome brick bands, terracotta mouldings and bay windows; chimney stacks with pots; wrought-iron railings; coloured painted shop-fronts and fascia boards.

style.vernacular: Steep, green peninsula city between the Lion Mountains and the Atlantic: dense hillside settlement of concrete-block and rendered houses with rusting corrugated-iron roofs, older Krio 'bod ose' board houses (stone ground floor, timber weatherboard upper floors, verandas) in the centre, Georgian-era churches and Victorian public buildings downtown, and more recent concrete civic blocks and hotels along the Aberdeen/Lumley coast. Red laterite ground, palms, mango and kapok trees.
style.ornament: Krio board houses with timber weatherboard cladding, shuttered sash windows, front verandas and fretwork; whitewashed stone churches with square towers and Georgian proportions; King's Yard Gate stone; the kapok Cotton Tree as the city emblem; hand-painted shop signage and bright market umbrellas.
